# UD Chechen MottDT

Language: [Chechen](/ce/index.html) (code: `ce`)<br/>
Family: Nakh-Daghestanian

This treebank has been part of Universal Dependencies since the UD v2.19 release.

The following people have contributed to making this treebank part of UD: Anna Veselovsky, Zarina Molochieva, Alena Witzlack-Makarevich.

Repository: [UD_Chechen-MottDT](https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Chechen-MottDT)<br />
Search this treebank on-line: [PML-TQ](https://lindat.mff.cuni.cz/services/pmltq/#!/treebank/udce_mottdt219)<br />
Download all treebanks: [UD 2.19](/#download)

License: CC BY-NC 4.0

Genre: spoken, grammar-examples

## Description

Chechen-MottDT is a Universal Dependencies treebank of the Chechen language (Nakh-Daghestanian).
The annotation for part of speech tags and features was coverted from interlinear glosses, while dependencies were annotated manually.
The treebank contains 3160 tokens.



The Chechen-MottDT treebank contains three oral folktales; the respective sentence IDs start with 'spoken'.
In addition, the treebank contains examples from the Chechen contribution to BivalTyp (the Typological Database of Bivalent Verbs and Their Encoding Frames).
The respective sentence IDs start with 'grammar'.
The texts included are as follows.

* spoken_bear: an oral folktale, 235 tokens
* spoken_wolf: an oral folktale, 668 tokens
* spoken_witch: an oral folktale, 1832 tokens
* grammar_examples: examples from the Chechen contribution to BivalTyp, 425 tokens

<h2>Syntax</h2>

<h3>Auxiliary Verbs and Copula</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 2 lemmas as copulas (<a>cop</a>). Examples: du, xila.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 2 lemmas as auxiliaries (<a>aux</a>). Examples: du, xila.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Core Arguments, Oblique Arguments and Adjuncts</h3>

Here we consider only relations between verbs (parent) and nouns or pronouns (child).

<h3>Verbs with Reflexive Core Objects</h3>

<ul>
  <li>This corpus contains 18 lemmas that occur at least once with a reflexive core object (<a>obj</a> or <a>iobj</a>). Examples: dilla shaa, lied'ala shie, aala shiega, aala shiiga, aeqqada shaa, aeqqada shie, da shiina, dala shiina, daqqa shaa, daqqa shie, daxa shaa, die shaa, die shie, diexka shie, dilla hwaigara, dilla shie, douza shie, ieqquo shie</li>
    <ul>
      <li>Out of those, 1 lemmas occurred more than once, but never without a reflexive dependent. Examples: lied'ala</li>
    </ul>
</ul>

<h3>Relations Overview</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 5 relation subtypes: <a>acl:relcl</a>, <a>advmod:emph</a>, <a>ccomp:reported</a>, <a>compound:redup</a>, <a>nmod:poss</a></li>
<li>The following 1 main types are not used alone, they are always subtyped: <a>compound</a></li>
<li>The following 6 relation types are not used in this corpus at all: <a>expl</a>, <a>clf</a>, <a>fixed</a>, <a>flat</a>, <a>list</a>, <a>goeswith</a></li>
</ul>
